records.real_world_identity_notes: The exact real-world match is Porsche's seventh-generation 911 Cup race car, the 911 GT3 Cup based on the 992-generation 911 and introduced for the 2021 season. It is a purpose-built, single-make GT racing car with a naturally aspirated 4.0-litre flat-six, six-speed sequential dog-type gearbox, electronic paddle actuator, and a driver-operated racing clutch. This is not the road-going 992 GT3, not the 991.2-generation 911 GT3 Cup 4.0 already covered elsewhere, and not a 992 GT3 R.

records.specification_basis: Porsche specifies a six-speed sequential gearbox, and the technical manual lists six forward gears and ratios 1 through 6. Porsche's summary calls it a sequential dog-type gearbox, and the exact technical manual repeats the construction as a sequential claw/dog gearbox. The sources identify right/left steering-wheel paddles and an electronic shift-barrel actuator for sequential gear selection. The exact technical manual calls the gearbox sequential and presents one right-paddle upshift path and one left-paddle downshift path. The car has a dedicated dry racing clutch and clutch pedal; the technical manual's neutral-to-first shift condition requires clutch pressure, establishing clutch use to engage first gear from rest. For the 1-to-6 upshift path, the technical manual lists the right paddle and no clutch pressure requirement. For the 6-to-1 downshift path, the technical manual lists the left paddle and no clutch pressure requirement. The driver-facing upshift is electronic paddle-actuated and the manual does not require a manual throttle blip for it; manual blipping is not the applicable control in this upshift path. The technical manual explicitly specifies an automatic blip in the 6-to-1 downshift condition, so the driver does not supply a manual throttle blip. The 1-to-6 upshift condition permits more than 30% throttle, so lifting off the throttle is not required for the documented running upshift. The manual frames the downshift condition as accelerator below 3% with an automatic blip; it does not define a separate driver lift technique beyond the normal downshift condition, so this field remains not-applicable under the project's sequential/auto-blip convention. The exact manual's downshift condition specifies the separate automatic-blip path and does not describe an automatic cut on downshift; this field is not applicable to the documented downshift behavior. The source specifies a driver-throttle/no-clutch upshift condition and does not describe an automatic blip on upshift; the blip function is documented for downshift instead. The exact technical manual labels the 6-to-1 downshift throttle condition 'Auto. Blip', directly establishing automatic rev matching on downshift. The full-resolution exact-992-Cup cockpit photo shows fixed molded grips at left and right around a central control face, and Porsche's launch material identifies the carbon-fiber motorsport wheel; this is the project's gt-formula category, not a continuous round or D-shaped band. The photograph shows the race display mounted behind the wheel, and Porsche places the 10.3-inch color display in the center of the dashboard rather than in the wheel itself. The photograph and Porsche description show an upper-open fixed-grip motorsport wheel. Under the schema's wheel taxonomy, open-top construction is not applicable to the gt-formula rim category. The full-resolution cockpit image shows no distinct shift-light strip on the wheel; Porsche's specification distinguishes illuminated push buttons from the separate dashboard display and does not identify wheel-mounted shift lights. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut.
